kurz: How twelve asset classes can be classified with three questions, and how the content of an investment differs from the wrapper in which it is sold.

bloecke.md:
The investment market seems confusing because it is organised by sales channel and not by effect. If you organise it by effect, every product can be captured with three questions.

1. The first question is where the return comes from. The possibilities are a contractually promised stream of payments, a share in the profits of a company or a property, or solely the fact that someone will pay more later.
2. The second question is what you are in legal terms: owner, creditor or contractual party. This determines what happens if the provider becomes insolvent, regardless of how the market performs.
3. The third question is when and at what price you can get your money back. Availability and stability of value are two different properties that are often treated as the same in sales conversations.

With the three answers, even an unfamiliar product can be classified. Everything else, such as the name, prospectus or product video, is packaging.

The **content** is the [[asset class]]: equities, bonds, property, commodities or bank deposits. It determines return and fluctuation.

The **wrapper** is the legal form of the investment: direct ownership, fund unit, certificate or insurance policy. It determines costs, tax and the ranking in an insolvency.

Two products with identical content can therefore differ fundamentally.

## Sources of return

There are three sources of return. **Contractual interest** comes from instant-access savings accounts, fixed-term deposits and bonds. Its level is fixed or linked to a reference rate. The risk is that the debtor does not pay or that nothing is left of the interest after deducting inflation. A **share in profits** is offered by equities, let properties and business holdings. Behind them is a company or asset that continuously generates surpluses. The level of the return is open, but it comes from these surpluses. The return on gold, commodities, crypto assets and foreign currencies is based on **pure price change**. These classes generate no cash flow; their entire return is the difference between two prices.

In practice, the difference shows in how strongly the result depends on the chosen starting year. After deducting inflation, gold has returned around 1.3% a year since 1900. Measured from 1977, shortly after the end of the dollar's fixed gold backing, the figure is around 3.3%. For an asset class without a stream of payments, the valuation at the starting point largely determines the result.

bloecke.md:
## The investor's legal position

An investor who puts money into an instant-access savings account lends it to the bank and becomes its creditor. The investor is protected by statutory deposit protection of up to €100,000 per customer and institution, so the limit does not apply per account. Securities in a securities account, by contrast, belong to the investor. The bank merely holds them in custody, so an insolvency of the bank does not affect the holdings. A fund launched in Germany, including an ETF, is as a rule held as [[Segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen)|segregated fund assets]] (Sondervermögen) under the KAGB (German Investment Code). These assets are kept separate from the balance sheet of the management company and do not form part of the insolvency estate if the management company becomes insolvent. For ETFs and other funds from Ireland or Luxembourg, the law of those countries applies. There, too, the fund assets are separate from the assets of the management company.

Certificates, warrants and ETNs are traded like other securities, but legally they are [[Bearer bond (Inhaberschuldverschreibung)|bearer bonds]] (Inhaberschuldverschreibungen), that is, unsecured claims against the issuer. If the issuer defaults, the money is lost, regardless of how the underlying is performing. The best-known example is the Lehman insolvency in September 2008.

- Deposit protection covers balances at a bank up to €100,000 per customer and institution. It does not apply to securities.
- Keeping the fund assets separate, which for German funds means holding them as segregated fund assets, protects investors in funds and ETFs against the insolvency of the fund company, but not against falls in the value of the fund's holdings.
- There is no such protection for certificates, ETNs and structured bonds. Here investors bear the issuer's risk in addition to market risk.

Without this distinction, an index certificate can easily be confused with an index ETF.

bloecke.unter: All four rows track the same basket of global equities. They differ in the investor's legal position, which decides the outcome if things go wrong.

bloecke.md:
## Availability and exit

[[Liquidity]] means that you can sell an investment without delay at a fair price. The fact that there is a market for it is not enough.

A flat can be traded, but a sale takes months. Incidental costs of between around 4.5% and just under 12% of the purchase price arise as soon as you buy: real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) ranging from 3.5% in Bavaria to 6.5% in North Rhine-Westphalia, Brandenburg, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein, around 1% to 1.5% for the notary and land register and, if an estate agent is involved, the agent's commission. Since December 2020, private buyers of a flat or a single-family house have as a rule borne at most half of this commission, so with a common total commission of 7.14%, that is 3.57%. The incidental costs are lost immediately after the purchase.

After the fund crisis of 2008 to 2010, in which investors lost €8.3 billion, open-ended real estate funds were given a minimum holding period of 24 months and a notice period of 12 months in the KAGB. Although the units are quoted on every trading day, the money is only available once these periods have expired.

A bond can be sold at any time, but not always at the purchase price. A ten-year German federal bond with a 2.5% coupon trades at 91.53% of its face value at a market yield of 3.52% (as of 18 September 2026); its modified duration is 8.61. If the yield rises by one percentage point, the price falls by around 8.2% to about 84.0%. The approximation using duration gives 8.6%; it slightly overestimates the decline for larger interest rate changes. An investor who holds the bond to maturity still receives the face value. If they need the money earlier, they bear the price loss.

bloecke.unter: Availability is plotted horizontally and price fluctuation vertically. Investments that are available at any time and fluctuate little earn less. Investments that are tied up and fluctuate strongly are particularly burdensome for investors.

bloecke.md:
For instant-access savings, the ECB deposit facility rate is the benchmark. It has been 2.50% since 16 September 2026. Banks pass on changes in key interest rates with a delay and only partially, and rarely pay more than this rate. 2.50% on €10,000 is €250. If the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) has already been used up by other capital income, €184 remains after flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) of 26.375%, that is, 1.84%. With inflation of 2.9% (August 2026), this gives a real return of 1.0184 / 1.029 − 1 = −1.0%. If the interest remains tax-free within the allowance, the real figure is 1.025 / 1.029 − 1 = −0.4%. The return is certain in nominal terms and just as certainly negative in real terms.

A ten-year German federal bond yields 3.52% to maturity, fixed for ten years. If the bond is held to the end, this yield is certain. If an investor has to sell in the first year and yields have risen by one percentage point by then, they sell around 7% to 8% below the purchase price, depending on the timing. A single interest rate move thus wipes out the interest advantage of just over one percentage point over instant-access savings.

A broad equity ETF promises no amount. The MSCI World returned around 8.5% a year net in euros from 1988 to 2025, and around 6.3% in the period 2001-2025. Between May 2001 and March 2009, the interim result was −53.6%. The expected value is the highest of the three investments, and so is the range of outcomes.

## Investment purpose and horizon

Before any purchase, asking when the money will be needed helps more than asking which class promises the highest return. The investment horizon rules out certain classes, and does so more bindingly than any personal preference. Since 1928, 26.5% of all calendar years of the S&P 500 have been negative. An investor who needs their money in two years therefore accepts a probability of around a quarter of having to sell at the wrong moment. Conversely, money loses purchasing power if it stays for thirty years in an account whose return after inflation and tax is reliably below zero.

bloecke.titel: Wrappers without an asset class of their own
bloecke.md: Endowment policies, unit-linked pension insurance, home savings contracts (Bausparverträge) and Riester contracts do not appear in the overview of asset classes. They are wrappers with their own tax rules and cost structures, whose content mostly consists of bonds and sometimes of funds. When assessing them, content and wrapper must be examined separately: the content for return and risk, the wrapper for costs, cancellation options and tax treatment. In advertising, the two are regularly combined into a single figure.

schritte.text: Establish which asset class the product contains. If this is still unclear after two minutes of reading the prospectus, that in itself is a warning sign.
The options are interest, a share in profits or pure price change. With a price change without cash flow, it should be clear who is supposed to pay more later and for what reason.
The possibilities are ownership, segregated fund assets, a claim or a contract. A look at the key information document, which must name the issuer, is enough for this.
Clarify when and with what notice period you can get out, what costs arise and what happens if you need the money earlier than planned.

bloecke.md:
After deduction of the saver's allowance of €1,000 per person, capital income is subject to flat-rate withholding tax of 25% plus solidarity surcharge, together 26.375%. Physical gold and crypto assets are exempt from this. They count as private disposal transactions (private Veräußerungsgeschäfte) under Section 23 EStG and are tax-free after a holding period of one year. Bringing the taxation of crypto assets under the flat-rate withholding tax has been announced, but was not in force in September 2026.

For funds, the **[[Partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)|partial exemption]]** reduces the tax base: 30% for equity funds, 15% for mixed funds, 60% or 80% for real estate funds, 0% for bond, money market and commodity funds. An equity ETF and a commodity ETC therefore differ in their content and also in the tax rate applied to the same result.

The overview shows how products can be classified, but not which one you should choose. It reliably answers three questions: where a product's return comes from, what it is in legal terms and when you can get out again. The fourth question remains open: how much money should go into which investment. It is dealt with in the following lessons and can only be asked sensibly once you can classify products.

A product on its own is neither good nor bad. What matters is whether it suits the purpose and horizon of the money. Most expensive mistakes arise from putting money with a short time frame into a class with a long horizon, rather than from an asset class that is wrong in itself.

mitnehmen: Every product can be classified by its source of return, the investor's legal position and the options for getting out.
A product's content determines return and fluctuation; the wrapper determines costs, tax and the ranking in an insolvency.
Deposit protection, segregated fund assets and issuer risk are three different levels, which is why an index certificate is legally something different from an index ETF.
Asset classes without cash flow, such as gold, commodities and crypto, only deliver the difference between two prices, so their long-term result depends heavily on the starting year.
The investment horizon rules out certain asset classes before the expected return even comes into play.

begriffe.text: Group of assets with a common source of return and a similar risk driver, that is, equities, bonds, property, commodities or bank deposits.

Assets of a German fund in contractual form, which under the KAGB (German Investment Code) are held separately from the assets of the fund management company and do not form part of the insolvency estate if that company becomes insolvent. For funds from other countries, such as Ireland or Luxembourg, the law of those countries applies.

Security that embodies a claim against the issuer. Certificates, warrants and ETNs belong to this category. If the issuer becomes insolvent, a total loss is possible, regardless of how the underlying performs.
The property of an investment of being exchangeable for money quickly and without a significant price discount. Tradability alone is not enough for this.

Share of an investment fund's income that is exempt from flat-rate withholding tax. It is 30% for equity funds, 15% for mixed funds, 60% or 80% for real estate funds and 0% for bond, money market and commodity funds.
